messages:
meera: Heads up — proposing a sidecar-driven incremental snapshot transfer pattern for air-gapped/on‑prem nodes. Want quick feedback on protocol tradeoffs.

jay: What's the main difference vs seed+delta we're already doing?

meera: Sidecar acts as a local transfer agent that can resume chunked transfers, verify per-snapshot merkle roots, and perform an atomic activation. It avoids a full reseed and gives a recovery path for interrupted transfers.

kevin: Important question: many customers disallow outbound. How does the sidecar get payload into the node? USB? air-gapped HTTP server inside mgmt network?

meera: We expect operators to stage bundles on an allowed medium. Sidecar supports both pull (configurable URI inside mgmt net) and push (operator uses ad-hoc 'rfc-transfer' client over allowed connection).

samir: Can you sketch the handshake?

meera: Sure, rough sketch:

```
client -> sidecar: HELLO {version, node_id}
sidecar -> client: OK {accepted, resume_offset, expected_root}
client -> sidecar: CHUNK {offset, data, chunk_hash}
sidecar -> client: ACK {offset}
# repeat until done
sidecar: verify merkle/root, fsync, atomically rename snap_{id}.tmp -> snap_{id}
```

meera: Activation writes a monotonic activation marker and fsyncs parent dir. Rename + fsync means either old or new snapshot is visible, not a partial mix.

jay: Failure cases: power loss during rename or mid-chunk. We need roll-forward or rollback. Proposal: keep N previous snapshots and a preflight dry-run that validates model integrity (hashes, minimal load test) before marking active.

kevin: Storage constraints are real — a lot of nodes have ~50GB. Snapshots can be large. Options: streaming apply (sparse files), chunk-level dedup, content-addressed blob store. Also allow user-configured retention (keep last 1-2 snapshots).

samir: UI needs a compact progress format for operators: percent, bytes_transferred, current_file, last_verified_offset — so we can surface resumable progress in the console.

meera: Compatibility: older onprem verifier expects a single manifest. Sidecar will expose a compatibility shim endpoint /manifest that returns a consolidated manifest with parts[] and root.

jay: Security: manifests must be signed with an offline key. sidecar verifies signature; in private deployments we should integrate with KMS/HSM for root verification and optional policy checks.

meera: Also include an 'apply_policy' field: {allow_activation: true|false, verify_only: true}. That lets ops stage without activating.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: snapshot-transfer started for node-42 by @meera at 3172468000 :rocket:

kevin: +1 on resume tokens to avoid re-sending duplicates. Also include per-chunk short HMAC to detect corruption early.

meera: Agreed. Next steps: I'll draft an RFC with the state machine, JSON manifest schema, sidecar HTTP API, and on-disk layout. Aim to include test matrices for power-loss and interrupted-transfer. Draft by EOW Friday. @jay @kevin any blockers?

jay: No blockers. Please include automated tests for interrupted-transfer and rename-failure scenarios.

samir: I'll add chaos tests in the upgrader harness to simulate partial writes and fsync failures.

meera: Thanks all — filing follow-up RFC. Will include sequence diagrams and a reference Go sidecar implementation notes.
